newsitem.title: USA: US West power grid seen curbed for few more weeks.
newsitem.headline: US West power grid seen curbed for few more weeks.

text.p: The power grid serving the western United States will remain operating at nearly 65 percent of capacity for several more weeks while an investigation into the August 10 power outage continues, said Edison International's Southern California Edison Co.
"It is a matter of a few more weeks," said John Ballance, manager of system operation at Edison. "But that is dependent on identifying mechanisms to prevent a similar outage."
He added that Edison will not agree to raising the rate until reliability is assured.
Ballance noted that "everyone wants to resume" full transmission use, "because fuel dollars are at stake," but emphasized that further work needs to be done.
He explained that several other actions have also been implemented as a result of the outage.

These include upgrading of maintenance practices--particularly tree trimming; greater communication between power providers regarding disruptions; and a commitment by the Bonneville Power Administration, a federal power marketing agency in the Pacific Northwest, to a full system study of voltage support.

The August outage resulted from the failure of voltage support in the Northwest when several high-voltage lines in Oregon and Washington came in contact with trees and tripped off within a short period of time.
"Now, any 500-kilovolt facility outage--such as a line, a breaker or a transformer, is made known to other members of the Western Systems Coordinating Council," noted Ballance.
Edison, for instance, notified WSCC members Monday night when two of the three high-voltage lines linking its service territory to the Northwest were shut by a fire north of Los Angeles, he said.
